false_friends_top.form: Comparison-shaped glyphs: < > <= >= == != <=> <-> ; bare | (kets, table rows); > as a blockquote or breadcrumb (Home > Shop); emoticons <3 :) :( ; ||spoiler||
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: COMPARISON is a token (token.ts:69) with no parse path (ConditionNode is unused), and a stray > closes a capsule. The root becomes Prose and at least the enclosing top-level form is lost; how much survives varies. spw-syntax-validate prints a warning and counts the file as passed; --strict fails the run. The cut gate fails it (proseFallback, spw-cut-gate.ts:191-194). The warning points at the enclosing top-level frame, not the offending line.
false_friends_top.failure_mode: whole-surface degradation (loud in the gate, quiet in the validator's summary)

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_comparison: comparisons, kets, blockquotes, emoticons and table pipes go in strings. Thresholds go in ?match[band]{ "high" => … } arms. Relations are words ('below_t_c').
mitigation.lint_message: comparison '>=' at L:C is outside a string and turns the whole surface into prose — quote it, or move the threshold into a ?match arm
mitigation.door_text: One stray > or <= anywhere turns the whole file into prose. Quote anything you would read aloud as 'greater than'.

false_friends_top.what_spw_does: Only integers and point decimals are numbers (literals.ts:92-95). A leading '-' is a hidden lexer error and the sign is dropped: '-' is a ConnectorKind but missing from DEFAULT_CONNECTOR_MAP (profiles.ts:27-46). Exponents, suffixes, percents and comma decimals split silently. '+-' silently becomes a sum. Concise uncertainty becomes a Scope. € and £ are lexer errors. The validator, lint, fingerprint and LSP stay quiet; only the cut gate and 'spw inspect source --through tokens' report lexer errors.
false_friends_top.failure_mode: silent split or hidden lexer error

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_numbers: put signed, scientific, uncertain, percent, dated and localized numbers in strings, or in registry cells %ns.key{ value, unit, at, rel|abs, src, status } (contract.spw:85, :89). Write a quantity as .{ n, unit } (water.spw:139) and an exponent vector as up/down facets.
mitigation.lint_message: '-70' loses its sign (hidden lexer error) — write "-70" or put the value in a registry cell; '9,81' splits into 9 and 81 — use 9.81 or a string; '50%' leaves a loose % operation — write 0.5 or "50%"
mitigation.door_text: A bare number in Spw is an integer or a decimal with a point. Signs, exponents, percents, units, dates, times, currency and locale separators go in quotes.

false_friends_top.form: A colon inside a value: clock times, timecode, ratios, MATLAB/Verilog ranges, CURIEs, :hover, chat lines, multi-word titles, YAML front matter, 'CUT TO:'
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: The colon always binds. 06:30 becomes Bind(06:30); 01:00:00:00 becomes three nested Bindings; 1:1000, egf:egfr, button:hover and 1:10 become nested Bindings. An unquoted multi-word value keeps its first word ('@viewer_a: is this live?' keeps 'is'; 'Title: The Return' keeps 'The'). A trailing colon ('CUT TO:') or an empty key takes the next line. The validator prints a pass; the cut gate catches only the cross-line case.

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_colon: quote every sentence a person typed and every value that contains a colon. Keep an integer frame count next to a timecode string (drop-frame pattern).
mitigation.lint_message: binding value 'is' is followed by loose words on the same line — quote the whole value; '06:30' parses as a nested binding — quote clock times, timecode and ratios
mitigation.door_text: The colon is how Spw names things. If your value contains a colon or a space, put it in quotes.

false_friends_top.form: The # family: '# ' with a space (a note line, MARC blank indicator, '150# class'), '#word' with no space (a comment habit or hashtag), '#1' / '#35mm' / '#!3', hex colours, '## Heading', #include and #if 0
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: '#' followed by whitespace is a dropped inscription anywhere on a line, including mid-line, so it silently erases the rest of that line ('field: 245 1# $a Water' loses '$a Water'). '#word' is a resonance/tag Operation; '#note' is not a comment. '#it's' opens an unterminated string. Digit-led forms become prose payloads or shatter. '#ff8800' is a tag and '#3a3a3a' becomes prose. Tags are case-sensitive, so #BookTok and #booktok are different identifiers. apposition.spw:83-84 and contract.spw:44 forbid apostrophes in # lines, a stricter rule than the lexer actually enforces.
false_friends_top.failure_mode: silent data loss (inscription) or silent reinterpretation (tag)

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_hash: '# ' plus a space is a note the parser throws away; '#word' is a tag operator; never put a digit or apostrophe right after #. Put colours in strings ("#ff8800" or a backtick phrase, as dusk-oak.spw does).
mitigation.lint_message: '#' followed by a space drops the rest of line N from the tree — move the data before it or into a string; '#ff8800' in value position is a tag, not a colour — quote it (3/4/6/8 hex digits only, to spare tags like #face)
mitigation.door_text: A # followed by a space starts a note the parser ignores, even mid-line. A # touching a word makes a tag. Numbers never follow #.

false_friends_top.form: = used for key=value, equations and assignment: .{ k = v }, .{ .x = 1 }, Size=Large, [size=large], revpar = adr*occ, E = m c^2, CHEMKIN 'A + B = C', dog=DEF, a gradebook formula
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: '=' is configuration, and a bare 'k = v' leaves three flat siblings with no Binding. Canon writes its own tables this way: materials-ontology.spw has 0 Bindings in 457 nodes, and operators.spw:28-42 uses the same form. Equations split; CHEMKIN '=' and '=>' split with no error. The tight '=~…[axis]{…}' form is a bias edge, which is a different thing again.

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_equals: Spw binds with a colon. '=' configures a register or opens a bias edge. Equations go in backtick 'form:' phrases next to unit-bearing registry cells.
mitigation.lint_message: 'k = v' inside .{ } forms no binding — write 'k: v' (designated initializers, TOML, Figma Property=Value and CHEMKIN '=' all land here)
mitigation.door_text: Write name: value. Keep equations in backtick phrases; Spw will not compute them.

false_friends_top.form: Spaced infix and line-end operators that grab their neighbours: x^2, a ^ b, ^H / H^ / ^wbc at line end, y ~ x1 + x2, a ~ b, p & q, a && b, x * y, n % 2, a <> b, adr: $180, A @ B, x: a ? b : c
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: Spw operators are prefixes. An identifier after a spaced bare operator becomes that operator's modifier. A caret label at the end of a line takes the next line's key as its subject. A ternary turns into two Bindings. All of these give a complete parse with no warning, and the cut gate passes them.
false_friends_top.failure_mode: silent restructuring (a complete parse that means something else)

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_infix: maths, formulas and code go in backtick phrases or strings; structure goes in facets such as .{ symbol: H, hat: true }; coupling is written in prefix form <>[a, b].
mitigation.lint_message: operator '^' at the end of line N takes the next line's key as its subject — quote the expression; 'x1' after a bare '~' becomes a modifier — a formula belongs in a backtick phrase
mitigation.door_text: Spw operators come before what they act on. Write your formulas in backticks; the tree keeps them intact.

false_friends_top.form: Line-end capsules, empty keys and URLs that swallow the next line: t: Vec<i32>, turnaround: 12<hours>, rot: 45<deg>, cold_open: 2<min>, a lone 'key:', url: https://…, the nine operator-angle cells (*< a >, $< a >, …)
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: A medial capsule that ends its line on '>' with no right arm takes the next line's key as its right arm. A key with no value takes the next line. In a URL, '//' starts a comment and leaves an empty binding. Infix shapes with a right arm on the same line, such as b<um>ili or A<f>B, are safe. The cut gate fails capsule and empty-binding swallows (spw-cut-gate.ts:207-211); the validator does not.

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_swallow: write durations as .{ n: 12, unit: "hours" }, quote URLs, end any capsule with a comma or a closer, and never leave a key bare.
mitigation.lint_message: value '12<hours>' ends line N on '>' and swallows line N+1 — end it with a comma or write .{ n: 12, unit: "hours" }
mitigation.door_text: A value that ends in > or : borrows the next line. Give it a comma, or use the .{ n, unit } form.

false_friends_top.form: Valence words boon/bane/bone/bonk/honk read as merit, status, sign or alarm (bane = error, inhibits, disputes, damaged; honk = alarm or hype; boon = success or glow; bone = incomplete), and used as keys
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: Canon calls valence charge-neutral material quality, 'not moral judgment' (valence-architecture.spw:38-39, :115). But canon's own wording invites the misreading: 'positive'/'negative' charge fields (:44, :53), 'glow' (:43), the electron-charge simile (:39). bias-product.spw:19 uses the pentad as edge direction, and mutate reads bane as 'revert'. catalog.ts:45-49 encodes bane as hazard/error, honk as telemetry alert, bone as incomplete and boon as completed deliverable. Used as binding keys (bone:, honk:), the words degrade the whole surface (contract.spw:146).

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/terms.spw#spw_term_valence: valence describes material quality, not merit. Never use it as pass/fail (dimensional-axes.spw:121). A refuted claim is #:claim #!refuted, never bane. Pathway or citation sign goes in the edge axis, never in =bane. The row should list your field's own 'valence' (combining capacity, vaccine -valent, ion z, affective valence, verb valency) as a separate word.
mitigation.lint_message: 'honk' is a valence modifier; used as a key it degrades the whole surface — rename it honk_cue, or use a string key
mitigation.door_text: These five words describe how a material behaves, not whether it is good. bane is a useful constraint, not an error. Your field's 'valence' is a different word.

false_friends_top.form: @ as a mention, 'at', a citation, matrix multiply or a handle: @ms_lee, @viewer_a, tod@s, @0800, '3 @ 5', lx_45 @ 70, @book{…}, @prefix, @angrist1991, A @ B, @the.author
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: '@name' is a Reference node (a root or alias); '@(…)' is the proposed perspective scope. Nothing is notified. spw graph turns '@k:' chat lines into root_shelves pseudo-nodes, so private names enter the tree against contract.spw:128 and :130. '@ 70' becomes a Reference named 70, and '@the.author' becomes a dotted path.

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_at: @ names a perspective or root. People appear as roles in strings; times as strings; citations as ~"registries/sources/…#src_" links; levels as plain decimals.
mitigation.lint_message: '@ms_lee' is a perspective/root reference, not a mention — name people by role in a string; '@ 70' after a value is a Reference named 70 — write level: 0.7
mitigation.door_text: @ notifies no one and is not a citation. Write roles, not names; write times in quotes.

false_friends_top.form: Typographic and non-ASCII characters outside strings: curly quotes and em dashes (Docs, Word, iOS Smart Punctuation, Scrivener, macOS), guillemets, accented keys (josé:, köy:), Greek and ħ/ℏ, \hbar, °, ×, ², ¿ ¡, € £, nº/№, emoji, IPA, arrows ↔ →
false_friends_top.what_spw_does: Each such character is a recoverable lexer error. Keys are truncated ('köy:' becomes 'kö' plus 'y:'); a curly-quoted value becomes an identifier; an emoji or 'ħ' can make an empty binding that swallows the next line. The validator prints a pass. The cut gate fails the file (contract.spw:153). Inside strings, backtick phrases and apposition bodies, all of these survive.

mitigation.glossary_entry: spw/glossary/false-friends.spw#spw_ff_typography: keys are ASCII slugs; people's words, accents, Greek and maths live in strings or apposition bodies. Name the smart-punctuation setting for each platform.
mitigation.lint_message: U+201C left curly quote at L:C — replace it with a straight quote; non-ASCII 'é' in a key truncates it to 'jos' — use an ASCII slug and keep the name in a string
mitigation.door_text: Turn off smart punctuation, or paste through a code editor. Keys are plain ASCII; anything in your own language goes inside quotes.

In a real cut the cells must move to registries/quantities/ for the gate to resolve them.

contraption_catalog.tooling_detail: Needed: an exact rational nullSpace(A) in packages/spw-seed/src/math/equation.ts (solveLinearSystem handles only square float systems), and a 'spw balance' or 'spw units' verb that reads %ns.key cells with up/down facets and hole sets. Also a gate rule tying each quantity cell to a dim link, and a charge row (charge_pos/charge_neg) for ionic schemes. Scratch prototypes exist: physics-tools/dim-check.mts, _ec_tools/contraptions.mts, social contraptions/run.mts.
contraption_catalog.wonder: A student watches permanganate refuse to balance, adds water, and sees the kernel appear. The same button finds Reynolds for pipe flow, flags the time dimension in coins per minute, and shows a household saving shock moving into the firm balance.
contraption_catalog.breaks: Homogeneity is not correctness: torque and energy share M L² T⁻², and radians are invisible. A balanced equation need not be feasible. theory_questions.question: Container deixis: should a particle run on the first line of a body bind to the enclosing frame (as catalogers, designers and crews expect, and as the LSP attributes it), or to the next child (as the seed does)? contract.spw:76 deliberately puts #:claim inside the claim frame, and the gate's source check (spw-cut-gate.ts:303-310) relies on that placement.

Is there, or should there be, a file-level deixis? The header stack binds forward to the ^"emit" card (contract.spw:45), while readers expect it to label the file, the way Rust's #![..] or #pragma once applies to the whole file.

Should case and mood names be allowed to start with a digit (#!3, #>12a, #!1a, #!42, #!5_point, NAICS, NGSS K-5 codes)? Or is the rule 'start with a letter or underscore' part of what makes a mood a word? Letter-led hyphenated codes already work.

Which names win for each aim? The lexer says deixis, case and mood; the LSP says anchor, lens and intent. Should docs keep the grammatical names, each paired with a closer term (index, attribute, value, stage)? 'Case' collides with switch-case and proof by cases; 'aspect' counts expiring content.
Is #! illocutionary force (sentence mood), epistemic status (#!settled), or a general value slot (#!field_guide)? If epistemic status matters, should it get its own case?

Which reader name wins for each split sigil: & subject or confluence, ^ ascension or integration, . ground or Subject, = configuration or Set, $ substrate or select? Canon itself is split (operators.spw:29-41 against operator-atlas.spw:41, math-modeling.spw:29 and flow-protocol-sigils.spw:34). Should physics homonyms keep their names with stated limits?

Is the operator × bound table meant to be total, so that every parsing cell eventually gets a reading, or are unnamed cells (*[ ], $( ), &( )) intended gaps? Is the ?< > wall (operator-atlas.spw:29 against the parser) a parser bug or a canon error?

Does the prefix-transitive / postfix-reflexive law (operator-atlas.spw:86-104) bind the parser? Today x!, x? and data~ parse as siblings. Is standby-then-go the motivating case for promoting ?'s proposed blocking strategy (operators.spw:147, :159-160)?

When canon writes === or 'theorem' for an operator law (wonder-calculus.spw:29-31, :56), which equivalence is meant: value, register writes, or trace? Should *~X === X be demoted to a proposed delay/force law, given that *{ ~{ x } } returns a deferred wrapper, and should & commutativity be stated per spelling?
Should Spw ever assert equality, commutation or isomorphism (a profile on <>, a 'commutes:' key, a witness-bearing iso form), or is 'pairing without identity' a deliberate stance?

Should infix 'a <> b' become coupling, and may <> be n-ary? Today the runtime couples only the first two string keys, bare identifiers count as keys, quoted operands keep their quotes, and a <> nested in #[ ] is never evaluated.

Are the register frame constructors #[ ] .{ } @( ) (operators.spw:93, 'Proposed') ready to promote? Is #[ ] unordered and unique by law, given that the AST keeps order and duplicates? ONF folds #[ ] items into metadata, and different probes report different ONF registers for .{ }.
Should the lexer own a list of compounds ($%, ##>, =>, <=>, <->) so compound notations get one clear reading, instead of splitting into siblings or degrading?

Reconcile three readings of the pentad: charge-neutral material quality (valence-architecture.spw:38-39, :115), edge direction (bias-product.spw:19, where mutate reverts bane), and catalog.ts:45-49 (bane = hazard/error, honk = alert, bone = incomplete). Canon's own 'positive/negative' charge fields (:44, :53), 'glow' (:43) and electron-charge simile (:39) state no limit. Should sign get its own words?
Should valence words be usable as binding keys (anatomy bone:, an SFX cue honk:, swatch names), for example by reading a modifier followed by a colon as a key?

Should the word 'valence' face chemists, clinicians, neuroscientists and linguists at all, given that each field already owns the word (combining capacity, vaccine -valent, ion z, affective valence, Tesnière valency)? Would 'material quality' serve science doors better?

Is the pentad ordered or categorical? Canon calls the combination a 'spectral signature' (:95, :100). Is identical share coverage a twin or the canonical ideal (:116, :140)? Can a surface carry two valences, for example a safety bulletin that is both honk and bane?

Canon says runtime quality is four-state BBBH with bonk as an overlay (valence-architecture.spw:31-34), but RuntimeValence = ModifierKind has five values. Has the :34 falsifier fired? Is the CSS and shader projection (--quality-* vars, :45-81, :120-131) normative, given that nothing in the repo defines those vars?

The bias axis is defined as 'which register is biased' (bias-product.spw:17), yet readers use it for relation types ([causes], [needs], [cites], [melts], [feeding]). Should bias axes get a declared closed vocabulary the gate checks? How should consumers avoid spw mutate --bias reading such edges as rewrite patches?
Canon documents a spaced bias form (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:37, :66; read-bias.ts:4) that yields no edge. Should readBias learn it, or should canon be amended to the subject-first tight form?

Should spw graph read bias edges as typed, directed edges and strip fragments the way the LSP does? Today it reports cyclic: #no for real cycles and lists valid #anchor targets as broken or as silent phantom nodes, depending on the working directory.

Is an anchor a place in a file or an identity that persists across dated editions? Should anchor uniqueness be scoped per edition (supersedes edges, delta by anchor) rather than cut-wide (spw-cut-gate.ts:202)?

Should citation typing (supports or disputes, aligned to CiTO) be edges or the canonical source/sources/counter bindings? Can a claim cite another claim and inherit its source? Should a proof inside the math domain count as a source?
Should emit continuity be anchored (#> anchors that a reader can link to) rather than prose phrases matched in the emitted text?

Is % one operator with several profiles — the [0,1] measure (wonder-calculus.spw:47), unbounded registry quantities (contract.spw:85) and count families (%mass) — or does the language need a quantity noun? Should unit-bearing KPIs and metrics become dimensional-axes 'axes' with domain and unit-or-ratio (dimensional-axes.spw:29-30), leaving %X for normalized measures?

Where do ordinal scores live (rubric levels, NEWS2 with its single-parameter trigger, Likert items)? As an ordinal measure family, or as ?match bands? Note that operational-field.spw:71 governs tool gating, not grading theory.
Should physical dimensions become checkable, with homogeneity as a falsifier (a dim link on every quantity cell)? Is a physical dimension an 'axis' in the dimensional-axes sense?

Will the lexer ever accept signed, scientific, uncertain or unit-bearing literals, given that '-' is declared a ConnectorKind but missing from the default map? Is there a time or timecode literal that cannot be read as a Binding, and how would it avoid colliding with clock names (operational-field.spw:48-50)?

Should 'illustrative' (a teaching number that asserts nothing about the world) be a claim status, and how does it sit with no_invented_numbers (contract.spw:81)? Should basis (what kind of evidence) and strength (how firmly to act) join #:claim?

~#lens( ) is parsed and counted by spw lattice but not indexed by the LSP (server-index has no APPOSITION branch), and the hover reads only '// lens:' (display.ts:304). Is lens meant to be tool-visible? Who owns the patch?

The lens set is closed and single-valued (vocabulary.spw:51; spw-cut-gate.ts:321-323). Should picture or representation readings get their own named apposition (~#picture( )), and which new lenses earn a place by recurrence ('symmetry and invariance', 'scale and dimension', 'equity')?

Do appositions compose, the way lens systems multiply or pictures transform? Is an apposition with no host valid? Should named appositions count as volatile 'aspect' (particles.ts:110-113, :129) in census and LSP volatility?

Is apposition the right home for scope notes and explanatory notes, or should 'gloss' (rejected at apposition.spw:52) return as a separate reading? Should theatre's 'aside' (rejected at :53 as connoting trivia) become a bridge row for theatre readers?

C-habituated readers: should Spw ship named prior-notation profiles (C, TeX, CSS, Stata/R, MARC, Markdown and chat, classroom) as revisioned semantics profiles (operators.spw:82, :89) that warn on familiar-but-wrong readings without changing the parse, following lint and -W flags?

Should one comparison, a stray >, or a blockquote degrade the whole surface, or should the failure stay local with a diagnostic on the offending line? Today the warning names the enclosing top-level frame.
Will the grammar adopt one same-line law, so that a medial capsule (Vec<i32>, 12<hours>), an empty binding, or a caret label at line end cannot take its right arm or value from the next line?

Is the tight-versus-spaced contrast (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:46-47) meant to change the parse, as it does now for bias and ~#k:, or only the reading confidence? C's '#define F(x)' versus 'F (x)' is the precedent for 'tight attaches'.

Should identifiers accept Unicode letters after NFC normalization, and should curly quotes and guillemets be string delimiters or named errors? Phone and Docs authors produce them by default, and ASCII-only keys silently truncate names like josé and köy.
Is the hyphen in identifiers (identifiers.ts:50) worth the collisions: a->b degrading, a-b as one name, x1-x5 varlists, and '- item' bullets?

Should '# ' (an inscription that drops the rest of the line, even mid-line) and '#word' (a tag) stay as they are? If so, should canon restate the apostrophe rule as 'no apostrophe or digit right after #', and should a C-habits profile flag '#word' at line start?

Clustering-oriented readers (physics, design, archives, crews): the cut says 'the tree is for finding, not for meaning' (contract.spw:137). Should facet axes (dept, season, era) and concept hubs become the main way to browse, with optional axes declared in the vocabulary? And how do readers whose tree is the meaning (syntax trees, finding aids) keep their structure?

Should '@handle: "text"' chat lines be a sanctioned surface form, or should people and roles have a construct separate from @ perspective, so that the privacy rule (contract.spw:128, :130) can be enforced by syntax?

limits.breaks: Not additive and not conserved. bonk has no free-energy non-analyticity, no control parameter and no first-order/continuous classification.

limits.observable: a Cartesian product of categorical axes
limits.breaks: At best a trivial product bundle over a finite base: no structure group, metric or connection, so no geodesics. It stays an analogy until the register-geometry.spw:26 falsifier is met.

limits.analogy: field as a physical field; schedule as operator splitting
limits.observable: scalar per site on a graph; ordered steps
limits.breaks: Explicit Euler on a graph, with no units. Directed diffusion is not guaranteed to conserve mass. The parser applies no step maps.

limits.observable: a labelled facet; a tag Operation; a tag or a prose payload
limits.breaks: No selection, cascade or specificity. #name is not unique. The parser never sees a colour.

limits.observable: @name(…){} with the first k: as Scope.name
limits.breaks: Nothing evaluates a condition. Range syntax (width >= 600px) degrades the file.

limits.analogy: Figma frames and layers; components and variants
limits.observable: nested ^ frames; spw expand inlines anchored regions
limits.breaks: No geometry, constraints or z-order. Figma lists the frontmost layer first and SVG paints later elements on top; Spw file order means neither. No overrides or variant resolution.

limits.analogy: x-sheet or timeline as composition order
limits.breaks: X-sheet rows are frames in time. Non-commutativity lives in transform stacks, parenting and rotation order, and over-compositing is itself non-commutative.

limits.analogy: kerning and Gestalt proximity as spacing
limits.observable: a tight bias edge exists; the spaced form yields none
limits.breaks: Proximity is graded; Spw spacing is discrete and position-specific. Canon reads the spaced form as softer commitment, not as no relation.

limits.analogy: valence as colour scale or shader
limits.breaks: Nothing in the repo defines them and no compositor runs. Hue is continuous and cyclic; whether valence is ordered is unsettled.

limits.analogy: golden grid as beauty or quasicrystal
limits.breaks: It shows aperiodic order, not beauty. Physical quasicrystals are atomic order seen in diffraction; the grid is additive, while a type scale is geometric.

limits.analogy: ^ as exponent or meet; ~ as equivalence
limits.breaks: No arithmetic or order. ~ is a unary operator, so relation axioms do not apply.
Closer to a probability or membership grade. No σ-additivity. Registry % cells are unbounded.
The intended law is delay/force (an inverse), not a duality, and it fails on value, writes and trace.
Body spelling: value depends on order. Frame spelling: writes depend on order. It is a band (last-wins) at best.

limits.observable: a closed table of four elements (⟨(12),(34)⟩ ≤ S4)
limits.breaks: An action on surfaces that does not preserve normal form. Equivariance on NF classes is untested (register-geometry.spw:116).

limits.analogy: -> as morphism; #[ ] as set; container stack as functor
limits.breaks: No types, identities or composition. Duplicates are kept and there is no comprehension. No morphism action is defined, which is the real reason against 'functor', not non-commutativity.
No meet, join or partial order. Of canon's crystal names, hcp is not a Bravais lattice.
No coefficients (a spaced 2 splits), no conservation, no K, rate or temperature dependence. An equilibrium holds between whole sides, not pairs of species.

limits.analogy: valence as chemical valence; bane as 'orbital boundary'; bonk as 'catalytic, precipitative'
limits.breaks: Not integers and not conserved. Electron density has no edge. A catalyst is regenerated unchanged. 'Ground state' adds a third 'ground'.

limits.analogy: . as electrical ground; & as mixing tee
limits.breaks: No reference potential. Physical mixing destroys provenance; Spw keeps it.
A balanced equation is not a feasible reaction. Torque and energy share dimensions. Ionic balance needs a charge row.
Polarity without dynamics (no gain, dead time or phase margin). Adjacency without geometry (no Clapeyron slope, no phase rule).
Sites hold unitless amplitude: no kilograms, moles or residence time.
Sign lives only in the axis; =bane means inverse lean, not inhibition. An edge is a claim in one context. Loop sign is necessary, not sufficient.

limits.analogy: valence as ion z, affect or alarm priority
limits.breaks: z is a signed integer; affective valence is a continuous hedonic judgment; alarms have IEC priorities. honk is attention without judgment.
NEWS2 is an ordinal sum from 0 to 20 with a single-parameter trigger, which normalization erases.

limits.analogy: field decay and beat as pharmacokinetics; membrane and flux
limits.observable: exponential decay; loading dose reaches plateau sooner
limits.breaks: fieldBeat decays every site, not just the central compartment. Transport is passive only, with no pumps and no electrical term (Nernst, GHK).

limits.analogy: capacity and affinity as Vmax and Kd
limits.breaks: Saturation is hyperbolic in [S]. Kd and Km carry concentration units, and Km ≈ Kd only under rapid equilibrium.

limits.analogy: <> as synapse or binding; schedule as care protocol; SBAR as a schedule
limits.breaks: Chemical and rectifying synapses are directional. Bundles have time windows and conditional steps. SBAR is a sender's template; read-back belongs to ISBARR.

limits.analogy: reference interval as registry constant; GRADE as #:claim
limits.observable: one value with tolerance; claim status
limits.breaks: An interval is a population percentile band set by lab and method. GRADE rates a body of evidence per outcome; 'settled' rates agreement.

limits.observable: binds the next node; resolved by ~"file#name"
limits.breaks: Holds as discourse deixis where it binds. When cited from elsewhere it is a coindex label, and the referent never shifts with the speaker.

limits.analogy: #: as case; #! as mood; ~# as aspect
limits.observable: role classifier; pragmatic force; volatility count
limits.breaks: No head and no government. Sentence mood holds, but the values mix status and genre. Aspect is event-internal time; expiring content is closer to stage-level.
Mostly a supplement rather than a coreferential appositive. An author is not a committed speaker, and host-hood is not checked.
Holds like an edge clitic in scope. No prosodic dependence, no syntactic choice of host, and attachment works across newlines.

limits.analogy: trees as ^ frames; feature matrices as facets
limits.breaks: No dominance, c-command or headedness. No unification, so conflicting facets coexist.

limits.analogy: rule ordering as sign × order; isoglosses for Spw naming
limits.breaks: Parallel OT has no order to permute. Spw names drift through one owner who can rename everything; the table records editing history, not diffusion.

limits.analogy: valence as valency; semantics and pragmatics as layers; register and dialect
limits.breaks: Valency counts arguments (ONF arity, operators.spw:81). The layer values do not match the subfields. Register also means a runtime slot and an ONF tag; a Spw dialect is a syntax gate.

limits.analogy: bias edge as regression coefficient or DAG arrow
limits.breaks: No magnitude, standard error or identification. 'Bias' here is not estimator bias or cognitive bias.
Transfer clamps at zero, while ledgers allow debt. A flows-only ledger is a sectoral-balance check, not stock-flow consistency, and the absorbing sector depends on the closure.
ADR and RevPAR carry units. Units cannot tell sold room-nights from available room-nights. NPS runs from −100 to 100.
Probes never run. The canon subjective-measure law governs gating, not whether Likert data is ordinal or interval.

limits.analogy: game table as periodic table; fixed point as equilibrium
limits.breaks: All 144 games are named, so a gap means incomplete coverage. Equilibria are fixed points of best-response maps, but reaching one is a stability question.

limits.analogy: resonance as correlation; spread as social distance
limits.observable: tags and identity locks; field extent
limits.breaks: Co-tagging is not covariance or a validated typology. Canon: spread 'does not measure … social proximity' (cli.spw:50).
A facet is the set of isolates from one train of characteristics. The closer form is #:axis #!isolate, and Colon Classification filing order also needs indicator ordinal values.

limits.analogy: bibliographic coupling as <>; citation as bias edge
limits.breaks: The corpus relation must be computed from source bindings. Anchored citation edges are read as rewrite patches by mutate.

limits.analogy: authority control as spw authority; fixity as spw cite
limits.breaks: spw authority reconciles writes and joins; spw cite prints a bytecode hash, not a byte digest.

limits.analogy: level of description as #:level; thesaurus as vocabulary.spw
limits.observable: reader level; closed sets with glosses
limits.breaks: #:level is target audience, not fonds or item. There is no BT/NT/RT among terms, no USE/UF, and scope notes exist per axis only.
The cut is an artificial collection. Document the arrangement as processing information; don't call it a fonds.

limits.observable: empty cells; adjacency under an order
limits.breaks: An empty cell predicts nothing about existence. Warburg's affinity is not a sort.

limits.observable: op:? before op:! in a Stream
limits.breaks: Runtime ? and ! neither wait nor fire. GO is said last; a standby blocks on a reply.
No clock, pre-wait or duration. One GO fires several cues as one event. A dissolve has a length that ~> lacks.
An anchor binds to a node, not a position. Digit-led names are invalid; spw graph reports false breaks.

limits.observable: product of side moods along cut order
limits.breaks: Moving cameras and lines change side mid-shot. The on-line setup has no inverse (a monoid). A matched pair sits on one side.
Lock is a promise to downstream departments. Continuity means matching across takes. Receipts record care applied to text, not the state of a negative or a lamp.

limits.analogy: craft scales (mireds, stops) as Spw measure; story beat as spw beat
limits.breaks: Gel 'halves' are product names, not half the mired value. Mired additivity is approximate on spiky spectra. spw beat is a clock with no story (field-dynamics.spw:53).

metaphor_limits.field: creators and media (authors, podcasters, live streamers)

limits.observable: tag op; Reference node; action op
limits.breaks: No feed, notification or execution. Tags are case-sensitive. Bare @ handles become graph pseudo-nodes.

limits.analogy: OBS scene as ( ); live stream as << >>
limits.breaks: No sources, layering or transitions. No clock. 'Stream' names both the broadcast and the AST node.
Audiences are not conserved. Diffusing across time-ordered segments has no meaning. Raids and co-host traffic are external inflow.

limits.analogy: chat clusters, format table, content calendar
limits.breaks: Chat is not a sample of the audience. A chosen axis predicts only what the chooser believes. Seasons are authored, not derived.

limits.analogy: valence as vibe; dashboard metrics as dimensions
limits.observable: material labels; num and den kind sets
limits.breaks: bane is a constraint, not bad energy. Platforms redefine metrics by policy (as_of plus version); counts have no SI dimension.

limits.analogy: lesson section as frame; agenda as schedule
limits.breaks: Frames carry no time. Nothing keeps time or runs the agenda.
A blank usually has one right answer; a hole matches anything. '___' is not a hole.
Rubric levels are ordinal. Equal spacing asserts an interval scale.

limits.analogy: prerequisite as needs edge; spiral curriculum
limits.observable: readBias ranked edge; concept cycle with rising rungs
limits.breaks: An authored edge is a claim about learners in general, not about each learner. Concept cycles are legitimate even though selector graphs must be acyclic.

limits.analogy: volunteers as field carriers; oral-history pairing
limits.breaks: People are not conserved mass. A shared noun is not a shared meaning, and only the teller can say which. The file records custody but does not grant it.

limits.analogy: glow-and-grow and boon-or-bane as valence; @-mention as @
limits.breaks: Valence is not merit. @ notifies no one and puts a person in the tree.

limits.analogy: materials-ontology.spw: ~ 'perfectly models latent heat'; * absorbs potential; $ 'meta-operator'
limits.breaks: No observable or stated limit (cli.spw:49). It contradicts operators.spw:29, :34 and :38, and its k = v facets yield 0 Bindings. Use it only as a contrast case.

limits.analogy: semantics-physics and register-geometry terms (spin, charge, fiber, tensor, geodesic)
limits.breaks: They stay analogies until domain, map, observable, invariant and counterexample are named (register-geometry.spw:26).
Not negation. The axiom it names fails at runtime.
A usefulness simile with no stated limit. It invites the merit reading that canon forbids at :38-39 and :115.
